name: Idaho
tagline: From Bear Lake and the Oregon Trail to Hells Canyon, the Sawtooths and Lake Pend Oreille.
intro: Idaho's byways climb the river canyons of the Clearwater, Salmon and Payette, cross lava fields and sagebrush desert on the Oregon Trail, and run beside the big northern lakes to the Canadian line. This chapter follows the Idaho Scenic Byways Program, run by the Idaho Transportation Department with the Idaho Byways Advisory Committee and listed by Visit Idaho, the state tourism office. Since 1991 the state has carried Forest Service and BLM routes under the same umbrella, so several backcountry byways on gravel are state members too.

members.name: Oregon Trail–Bear Lake Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the turquoise water of Bear Lake the road runs north to Montpelier, where Butch Cassidy's gang robbed the bank, then follows the Oregon Trail past the captive geyser at Soda Springs to Lava Hot Springs and McCammon.

members.name: Sacajawea Historic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 28 runs up the Lemhi River Valley beside the Continental Divide, past the old charcoal kilns near Leadore, to Salmon, where a center tells of Sacajawea and her part in the Corps of Discovery.

members.name: White Pine Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 3 leaves I-90 near the old Cataldo Mission, crosses lake-dotted marsh along the lower Coeur d'Alene River and the St. Joe at St. Maries, and ends at Potlatch, once a white pine mill town.

members.name: St. Joe River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Forest Highway 50 follows the St. Joe River east from St. Maries for 75 miles under cottonwoods where bald eagles and osprey fish, past the old Avery Ranger Station, then climbs north to the Montana line.

members.name: Ponderosa Pine Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 21 climbs from Boise to the gold rush town of Idaho City, follows the South Fork of the Payette past Lowman, and crosses Banner Summit, where avalanches can shut the road, to Stanley below the Sawtooths.

members.name: Wildlife Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Banks-Lowman Road follows the South Fork of the Payette River for about 36 miles through Garden Valley and Crouch, a whitewater and fishing canyon linking the Payette River and Ponderosa Pine byways.

members.name: Elk River Backcountry Byway
members.blurb: From Orofino the road crosses the North Fork of the Clearwater on the Dent Bridge, the tallest in Idaho, high over Dworshak Reservoir, then climbs through evergreen forest to the town of Elk River.

members.name: Lake Coeur d'Alene Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 97 leaves I-90 at Wolf Lodge Bay and winds south along the east shore of Lake Coeur d'Alene to Harrison, a winding two-lane road where eagle watchers gather in December and January.

members.name: Peaks to Craters Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Carey the road skirts the lava of Craters of the Moon, passes Arco, the first town lit by atomic power, and runs north through Mackay under Mount Borah, at 12,662 feet the highest point in Idaho.

members.name: Lewis and Clark Backcountry Byway
members.blurb: A single-lane gravel loop climbs from the Tendoy store to the Continental Divide at Lemhi Pass, through mountains and grassy foothills that look much as they did when Lewis and Clark passed in 1805.

members.name: Thousand Springs Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 30 follows the Snake River canyon from Bliss through Hagerman and Buhl to Twin Falls, past the waterfalls of Thousand Springs State Park and the fossil beds at Hagerman, with Shoshone Falls a short way off.

members.name: Teton Scenic Byway
members.blurb: On the quiet side of the Grand Tetons, the road runs from Swan Valley past Fall Creek Falls to Victor, then north through Driggs and Tetonia to Ashton, along an old Union Pacific spur now a trail.

members.name: Owyhee Uplands Backcountry Byway
members.blurb: Mostly one-lane gravel crosses about a hundred miles of high desert and juniper woodland on the Owyhee Plateau between Grand View and Jordan Valley, Oregon, with the Owyhee Mountains in view and few services.

members.name: Fort Henry Historic Byway
members.blurb: From Rexburg the road heads out to the white quartz St. Anthony Sand Dunes and north to Island Park, then returns along the Henry's Fork, a fly-fishing river, through St. Anthony and Chester to Ashton.

members.name: Main Oregon Trail Backcountry Byway
members.blurb: From Three Island Crossing at Glenns Ferry, one of the hardest fords on the Oregon Trail, about a hundred miles of road, two-thirds gravel, follow wagon ruts across the desert to Bonneville Point southeast of Boise.

members.name: Wild Horse Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 95 leaves downtown Sandpoint and runs north past McArthur Lake to Bonners Ferry, then Idaho 1 goes on to Porthill at the Canadian line, on a trail that served the Kootenai Tribe and later gold rush settlers.

members.name: Northwest Passage Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 12 climbs from Lewiston up the winding Clearwater River canyon to the Montana line on the route of Lewis and Clark, past Nez Perce historic sites, with a branch over the Camas Prairie to Grangeville.

members.name: Lower Payette River Heritage Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 52 leaves the Snake River at Payette and follows the Payette River east through orchard country and Emmett, past Black Canyon Dam, to Horseshoe Bend.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Mesa Falls Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Above Ashton the road climbs into the Caribou-Targhee forest to Upper and Lower Mesa Falls, each about ten stories high, where water spills over rock from an ancient super-eruption. In winter it becomes a snowmobile trail.

members.name: Western Heritage Historic Byway
members.blurb: Once a route for miners and homesteaders, the road runs from Meridian through Kuna and farm country into the Snake River Birds of Prey area, down to Swan Falls Dam and on to Celebration Park.

members.name: Payette River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 55 follows the Payette River north from Eagle through whitewater canyon, crosses on the 1933 Rainbow Bridge above Banks, and climbs past Cascade Reservoir to McCall on Payette Lake before ending at New Meadows.

members.name: Hells Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 71 runs west from Cambridge to the Snake River at Oxbow, then a road follows the Idaho shore down to Hells Canyon Dam in North America's deepest river gorge, country of bighorn sheep and bald eagles.

members.name: Snake River Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Back roads such as Map Rock Road and Chicken Dinner Road wind north from Walters Ferry through orchards and the vineyards of the Sunnyslope Wine Trail, above the Snake River canyon, toward Old Fort Boise at Parma.

members.name: Lost Gold Trails Loop
members.blurb: Old Highway 91 follows an early gold rush route north from Dubois to Spencer, where opals are still dug, then back roads cross east to meet the Fort Henry byway toward Kilgore.

members.name: Pioneer Historic Byway
members.blurb: From the Utah line the road runs north through Preston and Grace to Soda Springs and its captive geyser, near the old town site of Chesterfield, then climbs toward Wyoming on a stretch that heavy snow can close.

members.name: Salmon River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 93 follows the Salmon River south from the Montana line through North Fork, Salmon and Challis, then Idaho 75 turns west upriver to Stanley, with the Yankee Fork ghost towns of Bonanza and Custer nearby.

members.name: Pend Oreille Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 200 follows the rocky north shore of Lake Pend Oreille, the largest and deepest lake in Idaho, from Sandpoint through Hope and Clark Fork to the Montana line, with turnouts for the water view.

members.name: Panhandle Historic Rivers Passage
members.blurb: US 2 follows the north shore of the Pend Oreille River from the Washington line at Oldtown through Priest River to Sandpoint, past Albeni Falls Dam, in country scoured by the Ice Age Missoula floods.

members.name: City of Rocks Backcountry Byway
members.blurb: From Albion the road runs south through Elba and Almo to the granite spires of City of Rocks National Reserve, then follows gravel down Birch Creek to the historic district of Oakley.

members.name: Gold Rush Historic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 11 climbs from the Clearwater at Greer past grain fields to Weippe, with its Nez Perce and Lewis and Clark sites, and on to Pierce, where gold was first found in Idaho, ending at Headquarters.

members.name: International Selkirk Loop – Idaho Portion
members.blurb: The Idaho stretch of a loop through Washington and British Columbia runs from Oldtown up the Pend Oreille River to Sandpoint, then north through Bonners Ferry to Porthill, nearly all of it by river or lakeshore.

members.name: Sawtooth Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Idaho 75 runs north from Shoshone through Hailey and Ketchum along the Big Wood River, over Galena Summit and down to Stanley beneath the Sawtooths, in country kept dark enough for a night sky reserve.
